t: Beginning among Tamil poet-saints in the 6th to 9th centuries, the bhakti movement taught that loving devotion to a personal god is the surest path to liberation, open to all whatever their birth.
Its saints, women and low-caste artisans as well as Brahmins, sang in India’s spoken languages, not Sanskrit, and their songs shaped literatures from Tamil and Kannada to Marathi, Hindi and Bengali.
Never one organisation, it spread region by region over a thousand years, made devotion the centre of popular Hinduism, and some of its saints’ songs are preserved in the Sikh scripture.
dyk: Tulsidas recorded in the Ramcharitmanas itself that he began the poem at Ayodhya in 1574, on the festival of Rama’s birth; the Ramlila plays still staged across northern India each autumn are based on its verses.
ev: The Tamil Nayanars and Alvars compose hymns to Shiva and Vishnu and sing them at temples across the south
Nathamuni gathers the Alvars’ hymns as the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
Basava, minister at the Kalachuri court of Kalyani, leads the Virashaiva or Lingayat movement in Karnataka
Dnyaneshwar completes the Dnyaneshwari, a Marathi verse commentary on the Bhagavad Gita
Kabir, a weaver of Varanasi, sings of a formless God beyond the rites of Hindus and Muslims
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu becomes a renunciant and settles at Puri, spreading the chanting of Krishna’s names
Tulsidas begins the Ramcharitmanas, the story of Rama retold in the Awadhi form of Hindi
Death of Tukaram, whose songs crown the Varkari tradition of Maharashtra

f.where: Arose in the Tamil country of south India; spread to Karnataka and Maharashtra, then across northern India, Bengal, Odisha, Assam, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab and Kashmir
f.period: c. 6th–17th century: the Tamil Nayanars and Alvars c. 6th–9th centuries, Karnataka in the 12th, Maharashtra from the 13th, northern and eastern India above all in the 15th–17th
f.figures: Andal, Basava, Dnyaneshwar, Kabir, Mirabai, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
f.outcome: Made devotion sung in India’s regional languages the heart of popular Hinduism and founded lasting traditions, from the Sri Vaishnavas and Lingayats to the Varkaris and Gaudiya Vaishnavas
